To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) dual-mode contrast agents can provide a good balance of ultrasound and magnetic resonance enhancement, 2) the type of dual mode contrast agent and nanoparticle loading that provide the best contrast is that in which nanoparticles are loaded on the external surface of microbubble shell, 3) the use of low magnetic fields (0.25T) allows to obtain a good magnetic resonance enhancement without affecting the ultrasound signal, 4) low concentrations of dual mode contrast agents can provide the best contrast enhancement
the best results in terms of contrast enhancement are obtained by using modified microbubbles with a high density of superparamagnetic nanoparticles loaded on the bubble shell surface.
dual-mode contrast agents can be optimized in terms of nanoparticle density and shell composition to provide the best balance between ultrasound and magnetic resonance enhancement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of dual-mode agents able, in the future, to provide a more accurate and detailed diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases.
the development of innovative dual-mode ultrasound and magnetic resonance contrast agents, and with the identification of imaging parameters that optimize the dual-mode imaging performance.
the design of a new class of dual-mode contrast agent and with the development of an optimized imaging setup able to exploit the potentiality of the new agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a given type of dual-mode contrast agent, it is possible to identify the imaging setup parameters that optimize its detection with both imaging techniques.
dual-mode agents with nanoparticles anchored to the external shell surface offer a better balance between ultrasound and magnetic resonance contrast enhancement.
dual-mode agents based on gas-filled microbubbes with nanoparticles anchored on the shell surface provide the best contrast enhancement in ultrasound and magnetic ressonance imaging.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dual-mode contrast agents based on microbubbles with magnetic nanoparticles on the external shell offer the best compromise between magnetic resonance and ultrasonic contrast enhancement.
the use of dual-mode contrast agent is a promising approach for hybrid imaging, which is able to improve the contrast enhancement of both imaging modalities.

, by applying the appropriate setup parameters and imaging technique, the use of dual-mode microbubbles with a high density of superparamagnetic nanoparticles anchored to their external surface can be a valid alternative to the use of single-mode agents for medical applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to optimize the performance of a dual-mode agent by carefully tuning the imaging parameters.

dual-mode agents can be optimized for specific clinical applications, such as the detection of microbubbles in the blood stream, the detection of microbubble accumulation in the tumor or the detection of microvessels.
, in the case of dual-mode agents, the best imaging performance is obtained when nanoparticles are loaded on the bubble shell surface.
